items.prompt: Given an unsorted array, return true if any value appears at least twice.
items.why: Unsorted, no value range given, 'have I seen it before?' → one pass with a hash set. Cyclic sort needs values in 1..n; two pointers needs sorted input.

items.prompt: A sorted array and a target: return the indices of two numbers that add up to the target, using O(1) extra space.
items.why: Sorted input + O(1) space rules out the hash map; walk one pointer in from each end.

items.prompt: Group a list of words so that words made of the same letters (in any order) end up together.
items.why: 'Same letters, any order' → a canonical key (sorted word or a 26-count tuple) in a dict of lists. There is no window and nothing to enumerate.

items.prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum is exactly k. The array may contain negative numbers.
items.why: Negatives break the window's shrink rule. Count earlier prefixes equal to prefix − k with a hash map.

items.prompt: Find the length of the shortest contiguous subarray of positive integers whose sum is at least S.
items.why: All positive + contiguous + 'shortest such that' → dynamic window; no hash map needed because adding always increases the sum.

items.prompt: An array holds n numbers from the range 1..n; some appear twice and some are missing. Find all missing numbers in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
items.why: Values are exactly 1..n and extra space must be O(1) → put each value at its index instead of using a set.

items.prompt: Given an unsorted array, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers (their order in the array doesn't matter) in O(n).
items.why: O(n) forbids sorting; a hash set lets you start counting only at run starts (x − 1 absent).

items.prompt: Return the k values that occur most often in an array.
items.why: Counting is the first step, but the question is picking the k best by frequency → size-k heap (Top 'K' Elements).

items.prompt: Every number appears twice except one. Find the single one in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
items.why: A counter works but uses O(n) space; x ^ x = 0 cancels the pairs in O(1) space.
